upādānaparipavattasutta:
[Upādāna+paripavatta+sutta]  CL=9 This is a sutta where the Buddha declares that only when one thoroughly understands the four aspects of clinging (upadana), can one claim to have attained Omniscient Knowledge (sabbaññuta-ñāṇa). The four aspects are:
1. Understanding form (rupa)
2. Understanding the cause of form
3. Understanding the cessation of form
4. Understanding the path leading to the cessation of form
The Buddha teaches that only one who understands these aspects becomes:
- Well-established in the sasana (Buddhist teaching)
- Liberated from defilements (kilesa)
- One who has completed all spiritual tasks
The same pattern of understanding applies to the other four aggregates: feeling (vedana), perception (sañña), mental formations (sankhara), and consciousness (viññāṇa).'
This sutta emphasizes the importance of thoroughly understanding the nature of clinging through these four aspects for complete liberation. It"s worth noting that this systematic understanding of the five aggregates (khandhas) is crucial for achieving enlightenment.
